pages.name: Double it
pages.task: A resistor reads 6 V at 2 A, and its graph is a straight line through (0, 0). Which point is on it at 4 A?
pages.why: On a straight line through (0, 0), doubling the current doubles the voltage. 4 A is double 2 A, so the voltage is 2 × 6 = 12 V, the point (4, 12).

pages.text: A £40 call-out plus £30 an hour makes a straight line too, but it starts at £40. So 4 hours cost £160, not double the £100 for 2 hours.

pages.why: The line is straight, but at 0 m the empty drum already weighs 20 kg, so the line misses (0, 0). 20 m weighs 30 kg and 40 m weighs 40 kg, not double.

pages.name: Current up the side
pages.task: This graph has current up the side. Drag the point to show a 3 Ω resistor carrying 2 A.
pages.why: By V = IR, 2 A through 3 Ω takes 2 × 3 = 6 V. Current goes up the side here, so the point is 6 along and 2 up, (6, 2).

pages.why: Current is up the side here. At 30 V, line A carries 5 A and line B only 2 A. More volts for each amp means more ohms, so line B has more.
